summary_hint: Tells a processor which trust, who acts as trustee, and whether the trust may encumber the property.

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity — confirms this is the trust agreement vs a certification/amendment

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — preparing party (often counsel)

typed_core.name: trust_name
typed_core.why: identity — the trust the loan vests into

typed_core.name: trust_execution_date
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — which trust/version; distinguishes restatements

typed_core.name: trust_type
typed_core.why: processor — living/testamentary/land trust drives eligibility (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: revocable_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — revocable vs irrevocable headline (degraded from bool)

typed_core.name: governing_law_state
typed_core.why: processor — state law governing trustee powers

typed_core.name: tax_identification_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII (restricted); identity — the trust's TIN/EIN
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the trust TIN masked; never emit it to the catch-all

typed_core.name: grantor_or_settlor_name
typed_core.why: identity — who created the trust; match to borrower (flattened from person[])

typed_core.name: grantor_or_settlor_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — second grantor (e.g. spousal trust)

typed_core.name: grantor_or_settlor_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — number of grantors, so a bad name split is visible

typed_core.name: current_trustee_name
typed_core.why: identity — who can act for the trust; match to borrower (flattened from person[])

typed_core.name: current_trustee_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — second current trustee

typed_core.name: current_trustee_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — number of trustees / co-trustee acting requirements

typed_core.name: successor_trustee_name
typed_core.why: processor — who acts if the current trustee cannot (flattened from person[])

typed_core.name: beneficiary_name
typed_core.why: identity — who holds beneficial interest; match to borrower (flattened from person[])

typed_core.name: beneficiary_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — second beneficiary

typed_core.name: beneficiary_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — number of beneficiaries

typed_core.name: borrower_role_in_trust
typed_core.why: processor — grantor/trustee/beneficiary drives whether the borrower can pledge (degraded from enum)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish grantor/settlor, trustee, and beneficiary even when one person holds all three roles

typed_core.name: trustee_power_to_borrow
typed_core.why: processor — headline authority: may the trustee incur debt (degraded from bool)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Source each power flag to its granting clause; do not infer a power that is not expressly granted; record null when silent

typed_core.name: trustee_power_to_mortgage_or_encumber
typed_core.why: processor — headline authority: may the trustee pledge real property (degraded from bool)

typed_core.name: trustee_power_to_buy_sell_or_hold_real_property
typed_core.why: processor — real-property powers supporting the pledge (degraded from bool)

typed_core.name: distribution_terms
typed_core.why: processor — how/when the trust distributes (beneficial-interest context)

typed_core.name: subject_property_in_trust
typed_core.why: linkage — whether the subject property is (to be) held in trust (degraded from bool)

typed_core.name: trustee_signature_present
typed_core.why: execution — whether the trustee(s) executed the instrument (degraded/flattened from signature[])

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date, document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: a trust instrument is not a numbered/versioned form

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start/_end
rejected.reason: duplicate/derive from trust_execution_date; a trust has no statement period

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block, notary_acknowledgment
rejected.reason: trustee-signature presence captured; full notary block is low-value here

rejected.name: beneficiary_right_to_income, beneficiary_right_to_principal
rejected.reason: detail folded into distribution_terms; no rule

rejected.name: trust_asset_schedule, amendment_references
rejected.reason: genuinely repeat but not decision-critical; see Open questions

encoding_variations: Revocability stated as an explicit 'revocable'/'irrevocable' label, as a section granting the grantor power to amend/revoke, or implied by trust type — revocable_indicator beside trust_type disambiguates

Trustee powers appear as an enumerated powers list, incorporation of a state statutory powers act, or prose — the three power flags must each be sourced to the granting language; absence of an explicit power is null, not false
Trust name/date often restated by amendment ('the Smith Family Trust dated 1/1/2010, as amended') — trust_execution_date anchors the original
Grantor and trustee are frequently the same person in a revocable living trust — capture both roles even when names match

open_questions.q: Nested list for amendments. amendment_references determines which version of the trust governs — arguably the one structure worth nesting.
open_questions.recommendation: none now for a no-rule Tier-3 doc — flatten a count/latest-amendment date; revisit if a 'trust currency' rule is built GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Power flags degraded to str with null-when-silent. No bool coercer, and silence must not read as 'no power.'
open_questions.recommendation: confirm downstream treats null distinctly from 'No'

open_questions.q: More than two parties. Grantors/trustees/beneficiaries flattened to two + a count. Trusts can exceed two (multiple successor trustees, several beneficiaries).
open_questions.recommendation: flag when _count > 2 that the tail is in the catch-all; consider a person[] list only if a rule must address them individually GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

notes: The mortgage-relevant question is authority: can the trustee borrow and encumber the subject property. Source each power flag to its granting clause.
Do not infer a power that is not expressly granted; record null when silent (a rule/processor will treat silence as a gap).
Distinguish grantor/settlor, trustee, and beneficiary even when one person holds all three roles.
tax_identification_number_masked needs _PII_FIELDS registration, pre_masked true (a trust TIN/EIN, restricted); not covered by the registered employer_ein.
Ambiguity: subject_property_in_trust is tagged 'linkage' (not one of the five reason classes); mapped to reason_class 'identity' (identity/linkage to the subject property).
Ambiguity: trustee_signature_present is tagged 'execution' (not one of the five reason classes); mapped to reason_class 'processor' (execution status is a processor-facing verification concern).
